## Setup 1. Import this workflow, then open **Send Team Invite Email** and attach a Gmail OAuth2 credential (the same one used by the Proposal Email Delivery workflow works fine here too — it's just a second workflow using it, not a separate account). 2. Open **Team Invite Webhook** → Authentication is set to *Header Auth*. Create a new **Header Auth** credential: Name = `x-webhook-secret`, Value = any random string (can reuse the same secret as the proposal-email workflow, or use a different one — either works). 3. In the app's `.env`, set: - `EMAIL_PROVIDER=n8n` - `N8N_INVITE_WEBHOOK_URL=` - `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET=` (shared with the proposal-email workflow's env var of the same name) 4. Activate the workflow. This is a **separate workflow** from Proposal Email Delivery (not a shared one with a branch) so an approver's team-management activity — inviting people, resending invites — can be inspected, rate-limited, or changed independently of client-facing proposal delivery. The app already keeps them on separate URLs: `sendProposalEmail` posts to `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL`, `sendInviteEmail` posts to `N8N_INVITE_WEBHOOK_URL` (src/lib/email.ts). If `N8N_INVITE_WEBHOOK_URL` isn't set, the app falls back to `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` — so wiring only the proposal-email workflow still works, invites just also flow through it, exactly the shape it already accepts. ## Why this exists as its own workflow An invite email has no client, no attached document, and no CC list — it's one recipient, one link. Reusing the proposal workflow's node (which reads `body.clientName`/`body.proposalLink`/etc.) would work by accident since those fields are just left undefined, but a workflow that only reads the fields it actually needs is much easier to trust when someone opens it later wondering "what does this actually send." ## Payload this workflow expects ```json { "to": "newperson@example.com", "subject": "You're invited to Koya Talent Proposals", "html": "

...

", "text": "..." } ``` See `src/lib/email.ts` (`sendInviteEmail` / `sendViaN8nGeneric`) and `src/app/api/users/invite/route.ts` / `src/app/api/users/[id]/resend-invite/route.ts` — those two routes are the only callers. ## Response contract - `200 { ok: true, provider: "n8n", messageId }` - `403` — wrong/missing secret (handled by the Webhook node itself) - `502 { ok: false, error: "" }` Either response's detail ends up in the app: on `/api/users/invite` as the `emailError` field returned alongside the still-created account, and on resend as the `emailError` field too — never a silent failure, since a teammate who never got their invite is otherwise invisible until they ask why they can't sign in.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { ok: false, error: ($json.error && $json.error.message) || $json.message || "Failed to send email" } }}
